newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-WOODFORDE AND WOODBRIDGE WIN DOUBLES TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WOODFORDE AND WOODBRIDGE WIN DOUBLES TITLE.

text.p: Favoured
Australians Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge had only brief
problems before capturing their second Phoenix/ATP World Cup
Doubles Championship Sunday.
The Woodies, winning their 12th doubles title of the
year, turned back Texan Alex O'Brien and Canadian Sebastien
Lareau, 6 -4 5-7 6-2 7-6 (7-3) in a hard-fought final before
4,617 fans.
In addition to dividing a winner's prize of $165,000, the
Aussies gained an unprecedented sweep of the U.S. Open,
Wimbledon, World titles and Olympic gold in the same year.
The win also avenged a loss to O'Brien and Lareau in the
round robin of this competition on Friday.
"I guess it would be hard to top this year," said
Woodforde. "Maybe, we could play better next year and still
not win 12 championships."
In the end, it was the experience, consistency and
superior shotmaking of the Woodies that determined the
outcome. Only in the second set, when after leading 4-2 did
they show lapses that cost them the set.
With Woodforde serving in the 12th game, his team fought
off two set points before he volleyed out on the third to
make it 1-1 in sets.
"We decided after that set that when we hit with power
they were winning a lot of the points," said Woodbridge. "So
we tried to chip and make them play the soft stuff. It seemed
to help us."
Most of the remaining match belonged to the Australians.
At 1-2 in the third set, they ripped off five straight games
to take a 2-1 lead.
They were on top 5-3 in the fourth and final set before
Woodbridge was broken and the match went to the tiebreaker.
The Woodies went up 5-1 in the breaker and yielded only
two more points before running out the match when O'Brien hit
Woodbridge's serve wide.
"They play so smart and they cover each other so well,"
said O'Brien about his conquerors. "They play sweet tennis
and they pick you apart. They're one of the greatest doubles
teams ever.
"On the positive side for us, this is our first year as a
team and we didn't play our best tennis this week but we
still finished in the finals and ranked No. 4 in the world."
The losers split an $80,000 purse.
